description: The ratio divides each kept event name's average by the mean of the averages across all event names, the same baseline used for the filter.

b.request: Join budget lines to events (inner join, dropping budget lines with no matching event), compute each distinct event name's average budgeted `amount` ignoring NULLs, take the mean of those per-event-name averages (each name counted once), keep the event names whose average exceeds that mean, and for each show the event name, its average amount, the unrounded difference between its average and that mean, and the unrounded ratio of its average to that same mean
b.sql: WITH per_name AS (SELECT e.event_name AS event_name, AVG(b.amount) AS avg_amount FROM budget b INNER JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS mean_avg FROM per_name) SELECT p.event_name, p.avg_amount, p.avg_amount - o.mean_avg AS difference, p.avg_amount / o.mean_avg AS ratio FROM per_name p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_amount > o.mean_avg

a.request: Match budget lines to their events (drop budget lines with no matching event) and, for each event name, compute the average budgeted `amount`, ignoring missing amounts. Call the plain average of these per-event-name averages (each name counting once) the overall average, and keep only the event names whose average is above it. For each kept event name, show the event name, its average budgeted amount, its average minus the overall average, and its average divided by the average of the per-event-name averages taken over all event names (that is, the same overall average used for the filter). Do not round.
a.sql: WITH per_name AS (SELECT e.event_name AS event_name, AVG(b.amount) AS avg_amount FROM budget b INNER JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS overall_avg FROM per_name WHERE avg_amount IS NOT NULL) SELECT p.event_name, p.avg_amount AS average_amount, p.avg_amount - o.overall_avg AS difference_from_overall, p.avg_amount / o.overall_avg AS ratio_to_overall FROM per_name p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_amount > o.overall_avg

c.request: Using budget lines matched to their events (lines without a matching event left out), work out each event name's average budgeted `amount`, ignoring missing amounts. Find the event names whose average is above the average of the per-event-name averages, with each name counting once. For each one, show the event name, its average budgeted amount, how far that is above the average of the per-event-name averages, and its average as a ratio to the mean of these averages. No rounding. The ratio divides each kept event name's average by the mean of the averages across all event names, the same baseline used for the filter.
c.sql: WITH per_name AS (SELECT e.event_name AS event_name, AVG(b.amount) AS avg_amount FROM budget b JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_name HAVING AVG(b.amount) IS NOT NULL), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS mean_avg FROM per_name) SELECT p.event_name, p.avg_amount AS average_budgeted_amount, p.avg_amount - bl.mean_avg AS difference_above_mean, p.avg_amount / bl.mean_avg AS ratio_to_mean FROM per_name p CROSS JOIN baseline bl WHERE p.avg_amount > bl.mean_avg

d.request:
Using only budget lines that match an event (exclude lines with no matching event), compute each event name's average budgeted `amount`, ignoring missing amounts. Then compute the mean of those per-event-name averages, counting each event name once. Keep the event names whose average is above that mean. For each one, show:

- the event name
- its average budgeted amount
- how far its average is above the mean of the averages
- its average as a ratio to the mean of the averages, which is its average divided by that same mean used in the filter

Don't round any values.
d.sql: WITH per_event AS (SELECT e.event_name AS event_name, AVG(b.amount) AS avg_amount FROM budget b JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE b.amount IS NOT NULL GROUP BY e.event_name), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS mean_avg FROM per_event) SELECT p.event_name, p.avg_amount, p.avg_amount - o.mean_avg AS difference_above_mean, p.avg_amount / o.mean_avg AS ratio_to_mean FROM per_event p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_amount > o.mean_avg
